newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two Mexico crude ports closed amid high winds.
newsitem.headline: Two Mexico crude ports closed amid high winds.

text.p: Mexico crude ports Pajaritos in Veracruz state and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state were shut late Wednesday as wind speeds accelerated in the northern Gulf of Mexico to between 40 and 50 km per hour (about 25 and 30 miles per hour), port officials said Thursday.
Pajaritos shut Thursday at 2100 local/0300 GMT and Dos Bocas closed to petroleum exports at 1630 local/0030 GMT.
Port officials told Reuters the ports would be likely to reopen by Friday. Winds speeds were diminishing, they added, but waves were measured at a dangerous between eight and ten feet high.
The third and largest of Mexico's major crude ports was reported open Thursday amid the region's strong winds.
A cold front in the region closed northern gulf ports Tampico, Altamira and Tuxpan as of the Communication and Transport Ministry's 1500 local/2100 GMT meteorological bulletin on Wednesday.

Cayo Arcas ships 611,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude, Dos Bocas ships an average 440,000 bpd and Pajaritos ships 399,000 bpd according to the latest figures from state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
